conceptTitle: She Got On The Train With One Bag. He Didn't Know She'd Found The Messages.

footage.loopStrategy: trim first 5 seconds train night NYC

onScreenHook:
She got on the train with one bag.
He didn't know she'd found the messages.
She stared out the window for 40 minutes.
By the time she got off, she knew.
caption:
She found them on a Tuesday.

She didn't react. She put his phone down on the charger exactly where she'd found it. She went to the kitchen and started making dinner. She made enough for two.

They ate together. He told her about his day. She said the pasta was good.

She spent two days thinking.

On Thursday she packed one bag. Not a suitcase — a bag. Enough for a week. She moved slowly and deliberately, the way you move when you're trying not to think too fast.

She left in the morning while he was in the shower.

On the train she didn't cry. She watched the city lights blur past the window. She thought about who she had been at the beginning of this relationship and who she was now and what the distance between those two people had cost her.

She thought: the hardest part isn't the betrayal. The hardest part is the version of your life you have to grieve.

She got off at her sister's stop.

She knocked. Her sister opened the door and didn't say anything. Just stepped back to let her in.

She didn't go back.

Not because she couldn't. Because by the time she got off that train, she already knew.
